author: Alana Loftus
title: Trump signs historic Iran peace deal at Versailles, launching 60-day final agreement - NewsBreak
text:
By Alana Loftus ,
35 minutes ago President Donald Trump put pen to paper on the highly anticipated peace deal with Iran on Wednesday, marking the occasion with a ceremony at the Palace of Versailles.
The groundbreaking accord was completed during a dinner reception hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron within the storied palace walls. The deal officially brings closure to months of tensions between Washington and Tehran . Following extensive negotiations and numerous pledges that an agreement was forthcoming, Trump revealed earlier this week that terms had been finalized.
The White House shared that the U.S. president had signed the memorandum of understanding to conclude hostilities with Iran. Officials confirmed the pact is now in force, beginning an extendable 60-day window for the U.S. and Iran to hammer out a permanent settlement.

Trump affixed his signature alongside Macron and other distinguished guests. As he completed the signing, an attendee called out, "Bravo," sparking applause throughout the room, reports the Express US .
Secretary of State Marco Rubio stood nearby, collecting the document after Trump had finished signing.
On Sunday, Vice President JD Vance and Iran's lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf both electronically signed the memorandum, with Trump overseeing the process, according to a White House official.
According to the BBC, Trump departed the Palace of Versailles shortly past midnight following a dinner that lasted nearly two hours. Speaking to reporters as he exited, Trump declared, "It's signed. Signed in Versailles. Just signed it."
After revealing that a deal had been struck earlier this week, both Trump and Iranian officials indicated that a formal signing would occur sometime this week, and later suggested it might happen in Geneva on Friday.
It's still uncertain whether this plan will proceed now that the document has been signed by both sides. On Wednesday night, Trump departed Europe and returned to the U.S.
The peace agreement has been a central topic of conversation at the G7 summit this week. Trump has met with some of his closest allies, several of whom were vocal about their disapproval of the Iran war.
Before Wednesday's dinner at the renowned French chateau, Trump boasted about Macron's invitation, stating, "And then the French president, who happens to be a very nice man, invited me to dinner at Versailles."
Macron walked a fine line between criticizing the U.S. strikes on Iran during the conflict and holding Iran accountable for initiating the conflict. At the summit, Macron endorsed Trump's peace deal, declaring, "This is an agreement we support."

The groundbreaking accord was completed during a dinner reception hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron within the storied palace walls. Following extensive negotiations and numerous pledges that an agreement was forthcoming, Trump revealed earlier this week that terms had been finalized.
